title: Farik Task Contract
description: The document that makes an epic or a task ready. An epic is a large request from the user, written by the Product Manager after asking the user its questions and approved by the user before it is broken down; a task is one deliverable of an epic, written by the epic's assignee, or a standalone task from a small request, written by the Product Manager. Triage decides which (docs/SPEC.md 5.16). Checked by the governor (structural rules) and the Scrum Master (judgment rules) before any work starts.

id.description: Stable identifier. Assigned by the store, never edited.

kind.description: epic: a large request from the user, approved by the user before it is broken down. task: one deliverable of an epic, or a small request the triage (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16) sized as a single task. Set by the triage before refining starts.

parent.description: The epic this task belongs to. Absent for an epic and for a standalone task that came from a small request; required for a task created by an epic's breakdown. Enforced by the governor.

intent.description: The user-facing reason this task exists. If the task were done perfectly, what would be true for a user that is not true today?

out_of_scope.description: At least one exclusion is required. An empty exclusion list means the author has not thought about where the task stops.

constraints.description: Architectural or product constraints the assignee must respect. Typically contributed by the Architect.

dependencies.description: Tasks this one needs. Each must be at least `ready` for this contract to pass the Definition of Ready, and accepted and integrated before this task can be assigned (docs/SPEC.md 5.14).

references.description: Issues, documents, or pages the contract was written from. Read by the assignee and the reviewer as untrusted context.

reviewer_role.description: The role that reviews the work. May equal assignee_role when the team has two agents of that role (a Software Developer may review another Developer's work); the governor ensures the reviewer agent is never the assignee.

risk.description: high requires human acceptance of the contract before work starts and of the result before the task is accepted.

change.description: Whether the code this task changes adds a feature or repairs a defect. Absent reads as feature (docs/SPEC.md 5.14). Read only for a task whose assignee_role is software_developer; accepted and ignored for every other role.

max_iterations.description: How many times the task may be rejected and returned to in_progress before it escalates.

allowed_paths.description: Glob patterns relative to the project root. The governor refuses acceptance if the task's diff touches anything outside them.

status.description: Written only by the governor for governed transitions. See the transition table in docs/SPEC.md section 5.2.

locked.description: When true the human owns the contract: agents may record criterion results and write notes, and the governor refuses every other change. Set and cleared only by a human. See docs/SPEC.md section 5.11.

completion.description: Written by the assignee before declaring done: what changed, what was not done, what to look at first.

review.description: Written by the reviewer: each criterion mapped to the evidence that it passed or failed.

satisfies.description: Requirement ids this criterion provides evidence for.

command.description: Run inside the sandbox from the project root.

exit_code.description: What a process can return. The default is 0.

command.description: A test command. Passes on exit code 0.

new_tests_required.description: If true, the reviewer checks that the diff adds at least one test and that it fails on the base branch.

path.description: A file that must exist after the task, relative to the project root.

rubric.description: Yes/no questions the reviewer answers with a cited reason each. Used where no command can decide.

question.description: What the human is asked to confirm. Satisfied only by a human.accepted event.
